This vignette illustrates a compact workflow using the `bison` data included in
CircularRegression. The response `y.dir` is the movement direction at the
current time. The covariate `y.prec` is the previous movement direction, and
`x.meadow:z.meadow` represents the direction toward the nearest meadow weighted
by the associated non-negative distance variable.

```{r}
library(CircularRegression)

data(bison)

d <- bison[seq_len(200), c("y.dir", "y.prec", "x.meadow", "z.meadow")]
d <- na.omit(d)
str(d)
```

## Fit the default two-step model

```{r}
fit <- circular_regression(
  y.dir ~ y.prec + x.meadow:z.meadow,
  data = d
)

fit
```

The default fit selects a reference by empirical mean cosine and uses the
consensus coefficients to initialize the homogeneous angular fit. The
direction/modifier term asks whether the meadow direction contributes beyond
the previous heading. These first 200 records illustrate the software, not a
new ecological analysis of the entire trajectory.

```{r}
summary(fit)
coef(fit)
```

## Predictions and residuals

Predicted values are angles in radians. Residuals are wrapped circular
differences between the observed and fitted directions.

```{r}
pred <- predict(fit)
res <- residuals(fit)

head(data.frame(observed = d$y.dir, fitted = pred, residual = res))
summary(res)
```

A simple base-R diagnostic plot can be useful before calling the package plot
method.

```{r, fig.alt="Wrapped bison residuals against fitted movement direction, with a horizontal reference at zero."}
plot(
  pred,
  res,
  xlab = "Fitted direction",
  ylab = "Circular residual",
  pch = 19,
  col = "gray30"
)
abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
```

## Direct consensus fit

The consensus model can be fitted directly when the interest is in the
consensus coefficients.

```{r}
fit_cons <- consensus(
  y.dir ~ y.prec + x.meadow:z.meadow,
  data = d
)

coef(fit_cons)
head(predict(fit_cons))
```

This applied example is intentionally small so that it can be built quickly
as part of package checks. Larger analyses should keep the same structure:
inspect the angular variables, fit the model, examine circular residuals, and
verify that conclusions are stable under reasonable changes to the formula.

## Scope of uncertainty

```{r}
fit$convergence
fit$fit_status
fit$score_norm
sqrt(diag(vcov(fit, robust = TRUE)))
sqrt(diag(vcov(fit_cons, robust = TRUE)))
```

The two covariance summaries concern different probability models and coefficient scales.
The homogeneous model has a common concentration; the consensus concentration
is the fitted resultant length. Both sandwiches assume independent
observations. Movement records are ordered in time, so these standard errors
are not a substitute for modeling residual temporal dependence.
The distributed file contains processed data; raw GPS reconstruction is not
provided. All variables in this example use the documented radian convention.

This sequence can reveal unusual residuals and persistent temporal structure.
If either appears, investigate the affected records and the time ordering
before treating the printed standard errors as uncertainty for the trajectory.
Neither covariance here corrects residual serial dependence.
